nodes.name: Proposition 3.1: Smooth Decomposition
nodes.statement:
There exists a sequence of independent, stationary, centered Gaussian processes, denoted by $(\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))_{\boldsymbol{z} \in \mathbb{T}^d}$ for each $j\in \mathbb{N}\setminus\{0\}$, whose associated covariance kernels $\mathcal{K}_j$ and functions $K_j$ (as defined above) satisfy the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(P0)] (Smoothness). The sample paths of all the Gaussian processes $(\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}$ belong to $C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)$ almost surely.

    \item[(P1)] (Finite dependence). If $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z}, \boldsymbol{w}) \ge 3 \cdot 2^{-j}$, then the kernel $K_j(\boldsymbol{z}, \boldsymbol{w}) = 0$.
    
    \item[(P2)] (Sum to log-correlation). The sum of the covariance kernels is of logarithmic type:
    \[
    \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} K_j(\boldsymbol{z}, \boldsymbol{w}) = \log_+ \frac{1}{d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z}, \boldsymbol{w})} + g(\boldsymbol{z}\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}),    \quad \text{with $g \in C(\mathbb{T}^d)$.}
    \]

    
    
    \item[(P3)] (Limiting variance).  The variances of the processes, given by $\mathcal{K}_j(\mathbf{1})$, have the limit:
    \[
    \lim_{j \to \infty} \mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1}) =\lim\limits_{j\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{t})^2]=\log 2.
    \]
    
    \item[(P4)] (Uniform Derivative Bounds). There exists an increasing function $\Theta: (0, \infty) \to [1, \infty)$ such that for all $p > 0$,
    \begin{align}
        \sup_{j} \sup_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}| \le d} \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} \frac{\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]}{j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}} \le \Theta(p).
    \end{align}
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.4: Local Estimate
nodes.statement:
For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, we have the estimate 
\[
\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg].
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1: Fourier Dimension of GMC
nodes.statement:
For any integer $d\ge 1$, there exists a centered log-correlated Gaussian field on $\mathbb{T}^d$ with covariance kernel
	\[
	K(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w})=\log_+\frac{1}{d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w})}+g(\boldsymbol{z}\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{1}\},
	\] 
	where $g$ is a bounded continuous function on $\mathbb{T}^d$, such that for any $\gamma\in (0,\sqrt{2d})$, almost surely, the sub-critical GMC measure $\mathrm{GMC}_K^\gamma$ has Fourier dimension
	\[
	\dim_F(\mathrm{GMC}_K^\gamma)= D_{\gamma,d}\coloneq \left\{
	\begin{array}{cl}
		d-\gamma^2, & \text{if  $0<\gamma<\sqrt{2d}/2$},
		\vspace{2mm}
		\\
		(\sqrt{2d}-\gamma)^2, & \text{if $\sqrt{2d}/2\leq\gamma<\sqrt{2d}$}.
	\end{array}\right.
	\]
}

nodes.name: Proposition 1.2: $p$ -moment of $\mathcal{F}L^{\tau/2,q}$ -norm
nodes.statement:
For any $\tau\in (0,D_{\gamma,d})$, there exist $p$ and $q$ satisfying $1<p\le 2\le q<\infty$, such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[\|\mu_\infty\|_{\mathcal{F}L^{\tau/2,q}}^p\big]=\sup_{m\ge 1}\mathbb{E}\big[\|\mu_m\|_{\mathcal{F}L^{\tau/2,q}}^p\big]=\sup_{m\ge 1}\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big\{\sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d} \langle\boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau q/2}|\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})|^q\Big\}^{p/q}\Big]<\infty.
\]
